correctness.rationale: For a semigroup with zero, any k-complete mapping fixes zero and cannot encounter a nonzero k-th-power-zero element. In Rees zero-matrix multiplication, a zero sandwich entry supplies nonzero square-zero elements. When every entry is nonzero, all nonzero H-classes are groups and groupwise inversion is a global involution with x(f(x))^2=f(x). Explicit formulas and thirteen exact tests, including exhaustive small counts, confirm the boundary. The proof works over all finite groups, including nonabelian ones.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification of the first higher-power complete-mapping problem for the entire class of finite completely zero-simple semigroups, explicitly requested in the 2026 primary paper. The sharp threshold separates the existing sparse Brandt examples admitting k=1 mappings from the complete-support k=2 case, and the universal constructive inversion works over arbitrary groups. It is a structural result and not an arbitrary numerical sample.
